Adding driver's license digital version to iPhone is set to launch in the 15th U.S. state soon.

Apple currently lists 14 states that support the feature, plus Puerto Rico, and backend data shows another state will be added soon...

Many of us have long hoped to no longer carry physical identity documents such as driver's licenses and passports, but instead be able to present digital IDs directly on iPhone or Apple Watch.

This vision may still take a long time to realise, but Apple already took its first steps back in 2021, when the company announced plans to allow iPhone users to add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. To date, 14 states have adopted the feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend data discovered by MacRumors shows that Oklahoma will also join the list soon.

We previously provided a detailed walkthrough on how to add a driver's license or state ID to the iPhone Wallet app. As mentioned at the time, it should be noted that digital IDs cannot fully replace physical documents, so unfortunately we still recommend everyone to continue carrying a physical version.

Nonetheless, the digital version still helps protect your privacy—for instance, at eligible TSA security checkpoints, or when you need to prove your age to a merchant. The ID can confirm you meet the age requirement without disclosing any personal information, such as your date of birth.
